items.spec: 16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM (kept disabled), native USB-C
items.notes: Runs the firmware. PSRAM must stay off because its pins (GPIO 35-37) drive motors 6 and 7.

items.spec: Geared stepper, gear ratio about 63.7:1, about 4076 half-steps per output turn, up to about 15 rpm
items.notes: One per joint. Open loop: no position feedback, so joints are straightened by hand before power-up.

items.spec: 4 inputs per board, one board per stepper

items.part: 5 V power supply for the motors
items.notes: Close to the limit for 8 motors, so the firmware switches idle motors off.
Connects the ESP32-S3 to the computer. Power-only cables will not work.

items.qty: A few hundred grams per hand
items.notes: For the rigid skeleton. The 3D model works out to about 131 g of solid plastic; printed parts are usually lighter.
One closed loop per joint, wound on a 2 cm spool on the motor.

items.qty: A few grams per fingertip pad

items.spec: 5 V, serial bus (half-duplex), addressable IDs, position feedback
items.notes: Replaces the steppers in Phase 2. Daisy-chained on one cable and no manual homing.

items.spec: Connects the ESP32-S3 serial port to the servo bus
items.notes: Needed for the servo upgrade in Phase 2.

items.part: 5 V power supply for the servos
items.notes: Sized for 16 servos, split into 3 branches with capacitors. The 5 V / 2 A supply is only for the stepper prototype.
